description:
## What

`src/fetcher/cache.cr` has duplicate class-level and instance-level methods. Some are generated by a macro, some written out explicitly:

- Class-level (delegate to class store): `get`, `clear`, `clear_by_prefix`, `stats`, `enabled?`, `max_size` (6 methods, all generated by the `{% for %}` macro)
- Class-level (delegate to class store): `set`, `enabled=`, `max_size=` (3 methods, written out explicitly)
- Instance-level (delegate to instance store): `get`, `set`, `clear`, `clear_by_prefix`, `stats`, `enabled?`, `enabled=`, `max_size`, `max_size=` (9 methods, all written out)

The class-level ones are split: 6 are macro-generated, 3 are explicit. Why? Probably because the macro was added later, or because the explicit ones were added in a different commit.

## Why

Inconsistency. Reading the class, you see 6 generated + 3 explicit + 9 instance. The pattern is harder to see. Adding a new method requires knowing which side of the class/instance split it goes on.

## How

Either generate ALL class methods via the macro (consistency) or write them all explicitly. Macro is shorter; explicit is more searchable.

## Done when

- All 6+3 = 9 class methods use a single generation pattern (macro or explicit, not both)
- The instance methods are still 9 (no semantic change)
- Full spec suite still green
title: Refactor: unify Cache class-method generation (macro vs explicit)
